newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain regional debt up 11.4 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Spain regional debt up 11.4 percent in 1996.

text.p: Spain's regional governments increased their public debt in 1996 by 11.4 percent to 8.49 trillion pesetas, a Bank of Spain study showed.
That compares with a total debt of the Spanish central government of around 43.8 trillion pesetas at the end of 1996.

Of the 17 regional governments, Catalonia was the region with the highest level of debt, standing at 1.176 trillion pesetas. The Canary Islands had the fastest growing debt, which rose to 167 billion pesetas from 114 billion pesetas.

Even though the Bank of Spain said that the percentage of debt financed in bonos and bills in the market was rising, at the expense of a lower level of direct banking loans, this share still remained quite low.
Catalonia had, for example, a total of 366 billion pesetas in bonds and bills at the end of the year, while Andalusia had 466 billion pesetas.
Final 1996 deficit figures for different regions are not avaliable yet.
"In general we can say regional governments met their deficit target," the general director for the regional governments Enrique Gimenez-Reyna Rodriguez told Reuter.
